newsitem.title: USA: Dillon, SBC Warburg bond traders upbeat on merger.
newsitem.headline: Dillon, SBC Warburg bond traders upbeat on merger.

text.p: The details of the Dillon Read-SBC Warburg deal remain sketchy, but fixed-income employees at the companies were not overly worried about their jobs as a result of the proposed merger.
Sources on both firms' trading desks said the merger appears to be a positive move for both companies.

"Obviously there is uncertainty," said one trader, who wished to remain anonymous. "People are pretty cautiously optimistic. But we're not trying to focus on that because it will not happen overnight. It will be months before we get something final.
"Until then, I am going to trade, make money, and see how the cards fall," he added.
A source at the other firm said the mood was fairly upbeat. "I am not sure there is much overlap," he said. "People are very positive. It's a positive acquisition."
Dillon Read is the smaller of the two firms, with just 15 government traders and salesmen. Traders there said it is clear that the two companies are focused more on equities.
"The good people always remain," said one. "I am pretty confident in my abilities. We have a good trading desk. We are all going to be fine. Change is good."
Traders noted, however, that should the axe evenutally fall, they would no doubt find jobs elsewhere.
